app.description:
This App enforces the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org/) (DCO) on Pull Requests. It requires all commit messages to contain the `Signed-off-by` line with an email address that matches the commit author.


The Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) is a lightweight way for contributors to certify that they wrote or otherwise have the right to submit the code they are contributing to the project. Here is the full [text of the DCO](https://developercertificate.org/), reformatted for readability:

> By making a contribution to this project, I certify that:
>
> 1. The contribution was created in whole or in part by me and I have the right to submit it under the open source license indicated in the file; or
>
> 2. The contribution is based upon previous work that, to the best of my knowledge, is covered under an appropriate open source license and I have the right under that license to submit that work with modifications, whether created in whole or in part by me, under the same open source license (unless I am permitted to submit under a different license), as indicated in the file; or
>
> 3. The contribution was provided directly to me by some other person who certified 1., 2. or 3. and I have not modified it.
>
> 4. I understand and agree that this project and the contribution are public and that a record of the contribution (including all personal information I submit with it, including my sign-off) is maintained indefinitely and may be redistributed consistent with this project or the open source license(s) involved.

Contributors _sign-off_ that they adhere to these requirements by adding a `Signed-off-by` line to commit messages.

```
This is my commit message

Signed-off-by: Random J Developer <random@developer.example.org>
```

Git even has a `-s` command line option to append this automatically to your commit message:

```
$ git commit -s -m 'This is my commit message'
```

Once [installed](#usage), this integration will set the [status](https://developer.github.com/v3/repos/statuses/) to `failed` if commits in a Pull Request do not contain a valid `Signed-off-by` line.

![](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/173/24482273/a35dc23e-14b5-11e7-9371-fd241873e2c3.png)

GET repos/troupe-run/troupe/issues/442.body:
### What happens

`packages/troupe/tests/test_theatres.py::test_a_copy_that_differs_from_a_fresh_build_where_git_looks_compares_unequal[_make_an_empty_fan_out]` fails by chance. It failed on macOS with Python 3.12 in #441's CI ([job](https://github.com/troupe-run/troupe/actions/runs/44093042923/job/134073027297)), on a pull request that doesn't touch theatres:

```
    def _make_an_empty_fan_out(git_dir: Path) -> None:
>       assert not (git_dir / "objects" / "00").exists()  # no object of the copy's is named 00...
E       AssertionError: assert not True
```

### Why

The helper (added in 8ac91156) assumes the copied theatre's repository has no loose object whose hash starts with `00`. Commit hashes include the commit's time, so each run's objects differ. Each object has a 1 in 256 chance of starting with `00`, so with several objects in the copy, some runs fail.

### Done when

The test makes a fan-out directory that's empty, whatever the repository's objects are named. For example, it picks a two-hex-digit prefix no loose object uses, rather than assuming `00` is free. It no longer fails by chance.

A fresh build can't hide the result: if it has objects under that prefix, its directory is non-empty and left out of `_observed`, while the copy's empty one is counted, so the two still compare unequal. The new test writes the same real `00...` blob into both repositories from a file outside the worktree, asserts they compare equal, applies the helper, asserts the `00` directory still holds the blob, and asserts they compare unequal. pullRequest.body:
Closes #442

`test_theatres.py`'s `_make_an_empty_fan_out` assumed no loose object in the copied theatre is named `00...`. The commit's name follows its time, so about one run in 256 failed at the helper's assertion. This failure dropped #464 from the merge queue, and #466 reported it again.

- The helper now makes the first two-hex-digit prefix (`00` to `ff`) that the copy's `objects/` doesn't use. It checks the directory, not the kind of object in it, so a commit, tree or blob named `00...` is handled the same way. What the case proves is unchanged: an empty fan-out directory makes the copy compare unequal with a fresh build (design D1).
- A new test, `test_an_empty_fan_out_compares_unequal_when_an_object_is_named_00`, writes the same real blob named `00...` into the copy and into a fresh build. It checks they still compare equal, then applies the helper and checks they compare unequal. It needs no luck to fail (design D2).

Before the fix, the new test fails at the old helper's assertion:

```
>       assert not (git_dir / "objects" / "00").exists()  # no object of the copy's is named 00...
E       AssertionError: assert not True
FAILED packages/troupe/tests/test_theatres.py::test_an_empty_fan_out_compares_unequal_when_an_object_is_named_00
```

After the fix, all three fan-out tests pass, all 25 tests in `test_theatres.py` pass, and `scripts/check.py` passes (7148 passed).

This changes tests only, so there's no release and no milestone. The OpenSpec change `empty-fan-out` declares `skip_specs`, because no spec describes the theatres' comparison.
